name: 8051 Port Control Example
desc:
This is a simple 8051 assembly language program that creates a continuous loop to turn Port 1 pins completely ON and OFF. The program starts at the reset vector (address 0000H) and performs the following steps:

1. Turn all pins of Port 1 HIGH (ON).
2. Call a delay subroutine to create a visible delay.
3. Turn all pins of Port 1 LOW (OFF).
4. Call the delay subroutine again.
5. Repeat the process indefinitely using a short jump back to the start of the loop.

This program demonstrates basic control of I/O ports and the use of subroutines in the 8051 microcontroller.

files.sketch.asm:
;This program creates a continuous loop that turns 
;Port 1 pins completely ON and OFF. (To make this 
;visible on a real chip, you would normally insert 
;a delay loop between the states)

ORG 0000H
HERE:
MOV P1, #0FFH     ; Turn all pins of Port 1 HIGH (ON)
ACALL DELAY       ; Call a delay subroutine (assumed written below)
MOV P1, #00H      ; Turn all pins of Port 1 LOW (OFF)
ACALL DELAY       ; Call delay again
SJMP HERE         ; Short Jump back to 'HERE' for an infinite loop

; --- Simple Delay Subroutine ---
DELAY:
MOV R3, #0FFH
LOOP: 
DJNZ R3, LOOP     ; Decrement R3 until it hits 0
RET               ; Return to the main program

END
